title: Children of the Sea
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Ruka, a girl at odds with her school team and her parents, is drawn to the aquarium where her father works and to two mysterious boys, Umi and Sora, said to have been raised by dugongs. While the adults puzzle over fish vanishing from the oceans worldwide, the children are pulled into a mystery tied to the sea, myth and the cosmos (Viz blurb via AniList; ANN review).
life_message: Humans are part of a vast, living sea and cosmos, and wonder before nature matters more than control of it.

content.note: Little noted; ANN finds no violence in volume 1.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Gentle, slow-paced story; conflicts are everyday (ANN).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Ruka drifts free of school and parents over summer (ANN).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Family tension and new bonds with Umi and Sora (ANN).

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Adults only distantly aware; children lead the discovery (Viz blurb).

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Myth and mysticism over scientific explanation (AniList Mythology 94%).

folkways.japan: Summer by the coast, an aquarium and sea myths reflect Japanese coastal culture and a Shinto-like sense of a living ocean.

delivery.evidence: ANN calls the storytelling 'understated', with mysteries that unfold subtly.
delivery.note: Environmental and spiritual themes are left for readers to draw from images and mystery.

winners_losers: Ruka gains understanding and connection; no villains are noted. Sympathy goes to wonder before nature.
